newsitem.title: USA: Clinton must change budget -- Senate budget chair.
newsitem.headline: Clinton must change budget -- Senate budget chair.

text.p: Senate Budget Committee Chairman Pete Domenici said Tuesday that President Clinton must change his budget "dramatically," because it results in a large deficit in 2002.
Domenici said Clinton and Republicans in Congress both want to reach agreement on balancing the budget and that he still sees a potential for resolution.
But he said at a banking conference that he will be telling the White House formally that "they've got to do a lot better."
The Congressional Budget Office released an analysis Monday saying Clinton's plan would result in a $69 billion deficit in 2002.
Domenici, a Republican from New Mexico, said the proposed balanced budget constitutional amendment will not pass when it comes up for a vote in the Senate Tuesday.
"The bill is lost, we're going to lose by one vote," he said.

Many of the differences between Clinton's budget plan and how the Republicans view it is due to different expectations between the Congressional Budget Office and the White House Office of Management and Budget.
Domenici said that one area where the OMB is probably more accurate than the CBO is in estimating the amount of corporate tax payments to government.
